cards.q: 20 min in, it’s bad:
cards.why: We’d stay. They were brave enough to show up, so we can be kind until the bill.

cards.q: They reach for the bill:
cards.why: Let them. If they reach for it, that’s their gift, and the next one is on us.

cards.q: Great date, zero spark:
cards.why: Second date. Some sparks are shy, and a great date deserves a second look.

cards.q: Your friends hate them:
cards.why: Our call. We’d want to get to know them ourselves before we give up on anyone.

cards.q: They’re 25 min late, no warning:
cards.why: We’d give grace. Our own phones have died at the worst moment, more than once.

cards.q: Never have I ever said ‘you too’ when a waiter said ‘enjoy your meal’.
cards.a: I have, and I died inside
cards.why: We have. Politeness runs on autopilot, and our brains arrive a second too late.

cards.q: Never have I ever called a teacher ‘Mom’ or ‘Dad’ by accident.
cards.why: We have. Teachers looked after us all day, so our brains filed them under family.

cards.q: Never have I ever said ‘what?’ three times, then just laughed and nodded.
cards.why: We have. After the third ‘what?’, laughing along felt kinder than a fourth.

cards.q: Never have I ever turned up for something on the wrong day.
cards.why: We have. We saved the wrong date, then trusted our calendar completely.

cards.q: Never have I ever been annoyed at someone because of a dream I had.
cards.a: I have, they had it coming
cards.why: We have. We know it was only a dream, but we still needed a minute at breakfast.

cards.q: Messi or Ronaldo?
cards.why: Messi. He makes the impossible look like a kickabout in the park with friends.

cards.q: Is the Champions League better than the World Cup?
cards.why: No. Every four years, whole countries stop to watch the same match.

cards.q: Pep or Klopp?
cards.why: Klopp. We’d run through walls for a coach who hugs like that.

cards.q: Is a derby better than a final?
cards.why: Yes. A final is one night. A derby decides the mood at school or work all week.

cards.q: Can you hate a player and still love the game?
cards.why: Yes. Every good story needs a villain, and football writes the best ones.

cards.q: A whole cake appears in the shared fridge. No note, no name. Fair game?
cards.why: A whole cake with no note is usually someone’s surprise. We’d ask before we ruin it.

cards.q: A housemate’s grocery delivery arrives while they’re out. Put it all away for them?
cards.why: Ice cream waits for nobody. We’d put it all away and leave a note so they know.

cards.q: Something furry at the back of the shared fridge turns out to be yours. Admit it?
cards.why: We’d own it. Out loud, it’s a funny story. Binned in silence, it’s a house mystery.

cards.q: You’ve cooked way too much pasta. Knock on doors, or tomorrow’s lunch?
cards.why: Extra pasta is the best excuse we know to get the whole house around one table.

cards.q: Share a fridge with someone who never cleans it, or someone who ‘borrows’ your food?
cards.why: Borrowed food can be bought again. A fridge nobody cleans starts growing new housemates.

cards.q: Mom asks ‘Did you eat?’ What does it really mean?
cards.why: In our families, ‘Did you eat?’ is how love sounds when it doesn’t want a fuss.

cards.q: Calling each other out of the blue: lovely, or text first, please?
cards.why: Text first, please. A call out of nowhere makes us think something’s wrong.

cards.q: A selfie of you two: post it, or keep it between you?
cards.why: Just for us. Some photos mean more when only two people know they exist.

cards.q: Birthday messages between you two: a long, heartfelt paragraph, or short and sweet?
cards.why: The long one. Once a year, we let ourselves say everything we usually don’t.

cards.q: The photos on your phone: more of the other than they’d ever guess?
cards.why: Hundreds, honestly. Most are blurry and mid-laugh, and we can’t delete a single one.
